thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV2 - KV prefix cache runaway in us-east-1 (inference pool). Latency SLOs breached >20% for some customers. Paging maya (oncall) and tj (backup).

maya: I'm on it. Seeing a big jump in tail latency and memory on the batchers. KV cache sizes for some prefixes jumped 10x in the last 5m.

tj: grabbing graphs. Is this continuous-batching related or a separate cache key explosion? any recent deploys to runtime? 

maya: No runtime deploys in last hour. There was a prompt-template push from product that touched a couple of invocation templates ~12m ago. Could be template drift + hashing mismatch.

sophie: Dashboard: prefix-kv-cache hit_ratio collapsed, evictions spiked. Here's a quick summary: us-east-1: batcher-3 mem 92% -> OOM risk; per-prefix counts show many near-identical keys that differ by tokenization.

alex: can you paste an example key? i want to see tokenized vs raw prompt.

maya: sample from redis:

```
prefix::pfx_7f3a1c::tokens: "[101, 2023, 2003, ...]"
prefix::pfx_7f3a1c::tokens: "[101, 2023, 2, 3, ...]"
```

maya: looks like the tokenizer produced different token arrays for what should be the same canonical template (whitespace / unicode-normalization drift?). Keys not being normalized before hashing.

chris: that matches a regression I saw. We changed the tokenizer boundary handling in the tokenizer-lib upgrade (semver minor) — it normalizes certain punctuation differently. If prefix hashing uses token sequence raw bytes, small tokenizer changes = different keys.

tj: immediate mitigation options: 1) toggle prefix caching off for affected routes 2) quick patch: normalize inputs pre-hash to old behavior 3) purge bad keys (dangerous, could invalidate useful cache)

maya: cost/impact? turning caching off increases token compute but reduces memory pressure. Customers on Dedicated might need manual notification.

sophie: I'm drafting a quick status msg for CS. impact: approx 12 customers saw 2-4x latency increase for generation routes, 3 routes in us-east-1 primarily. No data leakage.

alex: I'll prepare a hotfix to revert tokenizer-normalization for the hashing path only (no full rollback). Patch snippet:

```
# hotfix: use legacy_normalize() before hash
def compute_prefix_hash(prompt):
    normalized = legacy_normalize(prompt)
    tokens = tokenizer.tokenize(normalized)
    return hash(tokens)
```

alex: I can push to canary in ~10m and toggle prefix-cache for canary routes to verify.

tj: also add a short-term autoscaler knob to increase batcher mem headroom and set continuous_batching=false for the most impacted routes to avoid oversized in-flight KV caches.

maya: doing a live toggle now: turning off prefix cache for route: /v1/generate -> done. Watching.

incident-bot: Deploy started: alex/hotfix-171980 - canary

maya: canary metrics look good so far — mem coming down, tail lat improving for that canary subset.

sophie: CS update ready to send. Calling out customers A, B, C as likely affected, recommending retry/backoff for a few minutes. Draft:

"We're investigating higher-than-normal latency for some generation requests in us-east-1. Root cause appears to be a caching key mismatch after a tokenizer change that increased the number of distinct prefix cache keys. We've applied a canary hotfix and toggled caching on some routes to stabilize latency. We'll follow up with a postmortem and next steps."

maya: alex -> push hotfix to region after canary green. tj -> coordinate on-call handoff in 35m. chris -> start a postmortem ticket, include tokenizer-lib change and template deploy.

alex: canary -> prod roll starting. rolling 3 hosts/region with replacement strategy.

incident-bot: Rollout complete for us-east-1. 3/3 hosts updated.

sophie: metrics: per-route p99 down from 1.8s -> 0.6s in 15m. KV cache cardinality halved.

tj: running a targeted key-clean script to remove clearly spurious tokenized variants older than 2h for impacted pfxes. Command used:

```
redis-cli --scan --pattern "prefix::pfx_*" | xargs -n 100 redis-cli unlink
```

chris: careful with unlink on prod, but ok for the identified keysets. ensure we only target keys with the bad tokenization suffix.

maya: script ran, removed ~42k keys from batcher-3. mem usage dropping.

sophie: sent CS update to affected customers with mitigation notes and ETA for full bake (1h). customers asked for root cause and whether they'll be billed extra; CS asked to confirm no data loss and that behavior returns to normal.

maya: confirm: no data loss. Bill impact minimal — small increased compute during mitigation window. please log the usage delta for billing.

alex: filing infra change to add a tokenizer hash compatibility test in CI for future token/lib upgrades.

tj: handoff: maya -> tj in 30m. summary pinned: KV prefix key explosion due to tokenizer normalization change + template drift; mitigated by hotfix to hashing path, toggling prefix cache and targeted key purge. Severity SEV2 -> monitoring.

maya: handing off now. i'll be reachable but moving to wrap up notes.

tj: taking over. will monitor next 2h and start postmortem doc. Good job team :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated. New incident ticket #INC-2024-1794 created. Follow-up: postmortem + CI test. Closure will be after RCA and customer comms.

chris: quick note for RCA - also confirm template deployment process (we should gate template pushes that change whitespace/normalization semantics)

sophie: adding that to the postmortem checklist. 

maya: thanks all. closing thread as mitigation is holding. we'll follow up with the write-up.
